answer: A lighthouse station gives each agent one numbered brass lantern, filled with a measured cup of oil at dusk and a wick trimmed to a marked length. The beacon beam sweeps the sea all night while the keeper logs each flame height in the tower book. At nadir, the darkest hour, a second keeper climbs the stairs and reads every wick number and flame against the log. Any lantern gone cold or burning below its mark loses its light slot for a month. A thousand fake keepers need a thousand lanterns lit all night, each with its own oil and its own climb at nadir.
